nodes.description: A copy-number gain of the 22q11.2 (LCR22A-D) interval — the reciprocal event of the 22q11.2 deletion — generated by non-allelic homologous recombination between the same flanking low-copy repeats. It raises the dosage of the interval genes, including the dosage-sensitive gene TBX1.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical variability of the 22q11.2 duplication syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The 22q11.2 duplication syndrome is an extremely variable disorder with a phenotype ranging from normal to learning disability and congenital defects.

Affected individuals are at increased risk for a variety of problems including gastrointestinal complications, endocrine dysfunction, ophthalmologic abnormalities, palatal anomalies, congenital heart disease, musculoskeletal differences, and neurologic abnormalities.

nodes.description: Increased dosage of the 22q11.2 interval genes (notably TBX1, dosage-sensitive for cardiac/pharyngeal development) drives a variably penetrant multisystem phenotype. Penetrance is markedly reduced, so the same duplication can be minimally symptomatic in one carrier and cause congenital defects in another.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical variability of the 22q11.2 duplication syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In a majority of the reported cases where parents have been tested, the duplication seems to have been inherited from a normal parent with minor abnormalities.
